question: The Shevaroy Hills are located in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Shevaroy Hills (Servarayan Hills) are a mountain range in the Eastern Ghats, located in Salem district, Tamil Nadu. (शेवरॉय पहाड़ियाँ — तमिलनाडु)

 

• The popular hill station of Yercaud is situated in the Shevaroy Hills, known for its coffee, orange and pepper plantations.

 

• The highest peak of the range is Servarayan (Shevaroy) peak, rising to about 1,620 metres above sea level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other hill ranges of Tamil Nadu include the Nilgiri Hills, Palani Hills and Anamalai Hills, all part of the Western Ghats/Eastern Ghats system.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 1): Known for the Maikal Hills and Bastar plateau, not the Shevaroy Hills.

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Known for the Eastern Ghats hill ranges such as the Niyamgiri Hills, not the Shevaroy Hills.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Known for the Aravalli Range, not the Shevaroy Hills.

question: In India Who among the following has the power to pardon, reprieve or commute the punishment of any criminal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 72 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of an offence. (राष्ट्रपति — क्षमादान की शक्ति)

 

• This power extends to cases where the punishment is for an offence against a Union law, cases tried by a court martial, and all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death.

 

• A similar but narrower power is vested in the Governor of a State under Article 161, except that the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The five forms of clemency available under Article 72 are pardon, commutation, remission, respite and reprieve.

 

• The pardoning power of the President is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, though the final decision rests with the President.

 

NOTE

 

• Prime Minister (Option 1): Heads the Council of Ministers but has no independent constitutional pardoning power.

 

• Attorney General of India (Option 2): Is the chief legal adviser to the Government of India; has no pardoning power.

 

• Vice-President (Option 4): Is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; has no pardoning power.

question: The “Nalacharitam” play is associated with which Indian dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• “Nalacharitam” is a famous Attakatha (Kathakali play script) composed by the poet Unnayi Variyar, based on the story of King Nala and Damayanti from the Mahabharata. (नलचरितम् — कथकली)

 

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form from Kerala, characterised by elaborate costumes, colourful face make-up, and stylised hand gestures (mudras) to narrate stories from the epics.

 

• Unnayi Variyar is regarded as one of the greatest Attakatha writers, and “Nalacharitam” (in four parts/days) is considered his masterpiece and one of the most celebrated Kathakali texts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other classic Kathakali Attakathas include Duryodhana Vadham and Kalyanasaugandhikam.

 

• Kathakali derives its themes largely from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavata Purana.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A classical dance form of North India, associated with storytelling through rhythmic footwork and spins; unrelated to Nalacharitam.

 

• Sattriya (Option 3): The classical dance form of Assam, originating in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) established by Sankardev.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): The classical dance form of Odisha, rooted in the traditions of the Jagannath Temple, Puri.

question: The President of which country attended the first Republic Day celebrations of India as its chief guest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indonesia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first Republic Day was celebrated on 26 January 1950, when the Constitution of India came into force.

 

• The chief guest for this first celebration was President Sukarno of Indonesia. (राष्ट्रपति सुकर्णो — प्रथम गणतंत्र दिवस मुख्य अतिथि)

 

• Inviting a chief guest for Republic Day, begun in 1950, has since become a regular diplomatic tradition symbolising India's friendship with the invited country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was sworn in as the first President of India on 26 January 1950.

 

• The Republic Day parade is held at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath), New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhutan (Option 1): Has never been the chief guest of India's first Republic Day.

 

• China (Option 3): Was not invited as chief guest for the first Republic Day.

 

• Japan (Option 4): Japan's Prime Minister was a chief guest in later years (e.g. 2014, 2015), not in 1950.

question:
Which of the following pair of compound – melting point is correct?

I. Acetic acid – 290K

II. Ethanol – 156K
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acetic acid has a melting point of about 290 K (16.6°C) — close to room temperature, which is why it is called “glacial acetic acid” when it solidifies in cold weather. (हिमीय एसीटिक अम्ल — गलनांक लगभग 290K)

 

• Ethanol has a melting (freezing) point of about 156-159 K (roughly -114 to -117°C), making it liquid across a very wide temperature range.

 

• Both listed melting points match the standard reference values used in NCERT-level organic chemistry tables for these compounds, so both statements are correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acetic acid's high melting point relative to other small organic acids arises from strong hydrogen bonding between its molecules (forming dimers).

 

• Ethanol's low melting point compared to its boiling point (351.5 K) reflects the weaker packing/ordering of its molecules in the solid state relative to hydrogen-bonded liquid ethanol.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect because it wrongly excludes ethanol's melting point, which is also correctly stated.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect because both given melting points are correct.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect because it wrongly excludes acetic acid's melting point, which is also correctly stated.

question: In India, what type of unemployment is created due to lack of employable skills among the educated youths in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Educated unemployment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Educated unemployment refers to a situation, common in India, where educated youths remain unemployed because they lack the skills demanded by the job market, or because their qualifications do not match available jobs. (शिक्षित बेरोजगारी — कौशल की कमी)

 

• It arises from a mismatch between the education system's output and industry/labour-market requirements, leading to underemployment or unemployment despite formal degrees.

 

• It is considered a distinctive feature of unemployment in developing economies like India, closely linked to the quality and relevance of education and vocational training.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Government skilling initiatives such as Skill India Mission and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) aim to address educated/skill-mismatch unemployment.

 

NOTE

 

• Structural unemployment (Option 1): Arises from a mismatch caused by changes in the structure of the economy (e.g., shift from agriculture to industry), not specifically from lack of skills among the educated.

 

• Cyclical unemployment (Option 3): Arises from the business cycle — unemployment rises during economic downturns/recessions and falls during booms.

 

• Technological unemployment (Option 4): Arises when workers lose jobs due to automation/technological change replacing labour.

question: Indian boxers ______________ won gold medals at the 73rd Strandja Memorial Boxing Tournament, held in Sofia, Bulgaria in February 2022.
option_1: Manju Rani (52 kg) and Nitu (48 kg)
option_2: Nikhat Zareen (52 kg) and Nitu (48 kg)
option_3: Nikhat Zareen (52 kg) and Pooja Rani (48 kg)
option_4: Manju Rani (52 kg) and Pooja Rani (48 kg)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nikhat Zareen (52 kg) and Nitu (48 kg).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 73rd Strandja Memorial Boxing Tournament, held in Sofia, Bulgaria in February 2022, Indian boxers Nikhat Zareen (52 kg) and Nitu Ghanghas (48 kg) both won gold medals. (निखत ज़रीन व नीतू — स्ट्रैंड्जा मेमोरियल स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• Nikhat Zareen defeated a strong field including former Olympic medallists to clinch gold, an early highlight of her breakout 2022 season.

 

• Nitu Ghanghas also won gold in the 48 kg category, and Nandini Gupta added a bronze medal for India at the same tournament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later in 2022, Nikhat Zareen went on to win gold at the World Boxing Championships and at the Commonwealth Games, while Nitu Ghanghas also won gold at the Commonwealth Games 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Manju Rani (Option 1 & 4): She is a boxer in the 48 kg category but did not win gold at this particular tournament in this pairing.

 

• Pooja Rani (Options 3 & 4): An Indian boxer (75 kg category), but she was not the 48 kg gold medallist at this tournament.

question: Who was associated with the foundation of the Fergusson College?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fergusson College, Pune, was established in 1885 by the Deccan Education Society, founded the previous year (1884) by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, Vishnushastri Chiplunkar and Mahadev Ballal Namjoshi. (बाल गंगाधर तिलक — फर्ग्युसन कॉलेज)

 

• The college was named after Sir James Fergusson, the then Governor of Bombay, and was set up to provide affordable, high-quality education to Indians.

 

• Tilak taught mathematics at Fergusson College in its early years before he devoted himself fully to political and nationalist activities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Deccan Education Society also went on to establish other prominent institutions in Pune.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale, though not a founder of the Deccan Education Society, later taught at and was closely associated with Fergusson College as a professor and, subsequently, its principal.

 

NOTE

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 1): Known as the “Grand Old Man of India”, propounded the Drain of Wealth theory; not linked to Fergusson College's founding.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 2): Associated with Fergusson College as a teacher/principal, but not one of its founders; he founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.

 

• Lajpat Rai (Option 3): Founder of institutions in Punjab (e.g., associated with DAV College movement); not linked to Fergusson College's founding.

question: Name the Bhakti Saint from South India who was initially a Jaina and a minister in the court of a Chalukya king in the twelfth century.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Basavanna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Basavanna (Basava) was a 12th-century Bhakti saint and social reformer from present-day Karnataka, regarded as the founder/prime propagator of the Lingayat (Veerashaiva) sect. (बासवन्ना — लिंगायत संप्रदाय)

 

• He was initially associated with Jainism before turning to Shaiva Bhakti, and later served as a minister (treasurer/prime minister) in the court of the Kalachuri king Bijjala II, a dynasty that arose as feudatories of the Chalukyas of Kalyani.

 

• Basavanna championed devotion to Lord Shiva (as Ishtalinga), rejected caste distinctions and ritualism, and his teachings are preserved in Vachanas (devotional sayings in Kannada).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lingayats worship a personal Ishtalinga and reject Vedic ritualism, idol worship in temples, and caste hierarchy.

 

NOTE

 

• Karaikkal Ammaiyar (Option 1): A Tamil Shaiva Nayanar saint-poetess, much earlier than the 12th century, unrelated to Jainism or a Chalukya court.

 

• Eknath (Option 3): A 16th-century Bhakti saint of Maharashtra, part of the Varkari tradition, not associated with the 12th century or a Chalukya court.

 

• Tallapaka Annamacharya (Option 4): A 15th-century Telugu Vaishnava saint-composer, famed as the first composer of Sankirtanas at Tirupati, not linked to Jainism or a Chalukya court.

question: Which amendment of Indian Constitution removed the right to property from the list of fundamental rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 44th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights (it deleted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31). (44वां संशोधन — संपत्ति का अधिकार)

 

• It made the right to property a legal/constitutional right under the newly inserted Article 300A, meaning no person can be deprived of property except by authority of law, but it is no longer enforceable directly through Article 32.

 

• This amendment was enacted by the Janata Party government led by Morarji Desai, largely to undo some excesses of the earlier 42nd Amendment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment (1976), called the “Mini-Constitution”, added the words “Socialist, Secular” to the Preamble and curtailed judicial review.

 

• The 44th Amendment also restored some safeguards diluted by the 42nd Amendment, such as reinstating certain checks on the proclamation of Emergency.

 

NOTE

 

• 41st Amendment (Option 1): Related to raising the age of retirement of members of State Public Service Commissions/Joint Public Service Commissions.

 

• 42nd Amendment (Option 2): Added Fundamental Duties and altered the Preamble; did not remove the right to property.

 

• 43rd Amendment (Option 3): Restored some of the judicial powers curtailed by the 42nd Amendment; did not deal with the right to property.

question: Who was the founder of Benaras Gharana of Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Janaki Prasad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathak, a classical dance form of North India, developed mainly into three gharanas (schools/traditions): Lucknow, Jaipur and Benaras (Varanasi).

 

• The Benaras Gharana of Kathak was founded by Janaki Prasad. (जानकी प्रसाद — बनारस घराना)

 

• The Benaras Gharana is distinguished by its own distinct style of footwork, use of both hands equally (unlike some other gharanas), and a repertoire without the use of “paran” in the same manner as other gharanas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lucknow Gharana was founded by Ishwari Prasad, and its style is known for grace, expression (abhinaya) and fluidity.

 

• The Jaipur Gharana is associated with Bhanuji, known for its emphasis on rigorous footwork (tatkar) and technical vigour.

 

NOTE

 

• Ishwari Prasad (Option 1): Founder of the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak, not the Benaras Gharana.

 

• Shambhu Maharaj (Option 2): A renowned Kathak exponent of the Lucknow Gharana, not the founder of the Benaras Gharana.

 

• Raja Chakradhar Singh (Option 3): A patron associated with the Raigarh Gharana of Kathak, not the Benaras Gharana.

question: What happens to the guard cells when water flows into them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stomatal pores open.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guard cells are bean-shaped cells surrounding each stoma (pore) on the leaf epidermis. (रक्षक कोशिकाएँ — रंध्र का खुलना)

 

• When water flows into the guard cells (due to osmosis, as solutes such as potassium ions accumulate), the cells become turgid and swell.

 

• Because the guard cells' inner walls (facing the pore) are thicker and less elastic than the outer walls, turgidity causes them to bulge outward, and this bends the cells, causing the stomatal pore to open.

 

• When water leaves the guard cells, they become flaccid, straighten out, and the stomatal pore closes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Stomata regulate gaseous exchange (CO₂ in, O₂ out) and transpiration (loss of water vapour) in plants.

 

• Stomatal opening/closing is influenced by factors like light, CO₂ concentration, temperature, and the hormone abscisic acid (ABA), which promotes closure under water stress.

 

NOTE

 

• The guard cells close (Option 1): Incorrect — water influx makes guard cells turgid, causing the pore to open, not the cells to “close”.

 

• Stomatal pores shrink (Option 3): Incorrect — shrinking/closing happens when water leaves the guard cells, not when it flows in.

 

• Stomatal pores close (Option 4): Incorrect — this is the opposite effect; closure happens on water loss (flaccidity), not water influx.

question:
The question consists of two statements, namely, Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Use them to choose the correct alternative.

Assertion (A): During the British rule, India’s exports exceeded the imports leading to surplus of balance of trade.

Reason (R): The surplus of balance of trade was used for growth and development of India.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: A is true and R is false
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true and R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true: During British rule, India consistently had an export surplus — the value of exports (mainly raw materials and cash crops) exceeded imports.

 

• Reason (R) is false: This trade surplus was not used for India's own growth and development. Instead, it was drained away to Britain to meet so-called “Home Charges” — payments for the India Office in London, salaries/pensions of British officials, interest on loans raised in England, and profits repatriated by British firms. (धन-निष्कासन सिद्धांत — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• This phenomenon was famously described as the “Drain of Wealth” theory, propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji in his work *“Poverty and Un-British Rule in India”*.

 

• Since the surplus was drained out rather than reinvested in India, A is true but R (which claims the surplus aided India's development) is false.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Drain of Wealth theory is considered one of the earliest economic critiques of colonialism in India and fuelled the growth of nationalist economic thought.

 

• Other early nationalist economists who wrote on colonial economic drain include R.C. Dutt in *“The Economic History of India”*.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Both true, R explains A): Incorrect because R itself is factually false.

 

• Option 2 (Both true, R doesn't explain A): Incorrect because R is not true at all.

 

• Option 3 (A false, R true): Incorrect because A is actually true (export surplus did exist) and R is the one that is false.

question: The Mauryan pillar capital found at ________ is popularly known as the Lion Capital.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarnath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lion Capital of Ashoka, found at Sarnath (near Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh), is one of the finest examples of Mauryan art, dating to around 250 BCE. (सारनाथ का सिंह स्तंभ — राष्ट्रीय प्रतीक)

 

• It consists of four lions standing back to back, mounted on an abacus carrying a wheel (Dharmachakra) and figures of an elephant, a galloping horse, a bull and a lion, separated by wheels, resting on a bell-shaped lotus.

 

• It was erected by Emperor Ashoka to commemorate the site of the Buddha's first sermon (Dhammachakra Pravartana) at Sarnath.

 

• India adopted this Lion Capital as the State Emblem of India on 26 January 1950, with the motto “Satyameva Jayate” inscribed below it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Only three of the four lions and the wheel from the original capital are visible on the state emblem; the fourth lion is hidden from view.

 

• The original Lion Capital is preserved in the Sarnath Museum, Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhabru (Option 1): Site (near Bairat) of a minor rock edict of Ashoka expressing his faith in Buddhism, not the Lion Capital.

 

• Bairat (Option 2): Site in Rajasthan with Ashokan inscriptions and a circular Buddhist temple, not the Lion Capital.

 

• Sanchi (Option 3): Famous for the Great Stupa and an Ashokan pillar with a lion capital, but the iconic four-lion Lion Capital adopted as the national emblem is from Sarnath, not Sanchi.

question: How many engines drive ‘PM Gati Shakti’, a project launched by the central government with an aim to revolutionise infrastructure in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PM Gati Shakti – National Master Plan for Multi-modal Connectivity was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 13 October 2021. (पीएम गति शक्ति — सात इंजन)

 

• It is driven by seven engines: Roads, Railways, Airports, Ports, Mass Transport, Waterways and Logistics Infrastructure.

 

• The plan aims to provide multi-modal connectivity infrastructure to various economic zones and reduce logistics costs, using a common digital platform (GIS-based) for integrated planning across ministries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Supporting pillars of the plan include Comprehensiveness, Prioritisation, Optimisation, Synchronisation, Analytical capability and Dynamic monitoring.

 

• It builds on the earlier National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) to ensure integrated planning and implementation of infrastructure projects.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (Two, Nine, Four): Incorrect — the officially stated number of engines driving PM Gati Shakti is seven, not two, nine or four.

question: Where is the National Dope Testing Laboratory located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) is located in New Delhi, on the campus of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). (राष्ट्रीय डोप परीक्षण प्रयोगशाला — नई दिल्ली)

 

• It is a WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency) accredited laboratory under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, responsible for testing samples of athletes for banned substances.

 

• It works closely with the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA), also headquartered in New Delhi, which is India's national body for implementing anti-doping rules.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NDTL was the first WADA-accredited laboratory in Asia.

 

• NADA India was established in 2005 to promote doping-free sport in India, in line with the World Anti-Doping Code.

 

NOTE

 

• Mumbai (Option 1), Bangalore (Option 2) and Punjab (Option 3): None of these host the National Dope Testing Laboratory, which is situated in New Delhi.

question: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ram Narayan was a renowned Indian classical musician celebrated as a Sarangi maestro. (पंडित राम नारायण — सारंगी वादक)

 

• He was the first sarangi player to give a solo classical performance of the instrument (which was traditionally used mainly as an accompaniment to vocal music), establishing it as a solo concert instrument both in India and internationally.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2005), in addition to earlier Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri awards, for his contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument widely used in Hindustani classical music, closely associated with vocal-style ornamentation (gayaki ang).

 

NOTE

 

• Ghatam (Option 1): A percussion instrument (clay pot) associated with Carnatic music; notable exponents include Vikku Vinayakram.

 

• Tabla (Option 2): A pair of hand drums; notable exponents include Ustad Zakir Hussain and Ustad Alla Rakha.

 

• Bansuri (Option 3): A bamboo flute; notable exponents include Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia.

question: In January 2022, the Supreme Court conferred daughters with equal right to the father’s property even prior to codification of Hindu Personal Laws and enactment of the Hindu Succession Act in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1956.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In January 2022, in the case of Arunachala Gounder (Dead) vs Ponnusamy, the Supreme Court held that a daughter has an equal right to inherit her father's self-acquired property, even if the father died before the codification of Hindu personal laws. (हिंदू उत्तराधिकार अधिनियम — 1956)

 

• The Hindu Succession Act was enacted in 1956, and this ruling clarified that a daughter is entitled to inherit intestate self-acquired property of the father, treating it as inherited by her by “survivorship” rather than only as per later succession rules.

 

• The ruling was significant because it extended the daughter's inheritance right even to succession that opened before 1956, reinforcing gender equality in property rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 had earlier given daughters equal coparcenary rights by birth in ancestral joint family property, further strengthened by the Vineeta Sharma vs Rakesh Sharma (2020) judgment.

 

NOTE

 

• 1959, 1952, 1947 (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these is the year the Hindu Succession Act was enacted; the Act was enacted in 1956.

question: Who coined the term ‘zeroth law of thermodynamics’ in 1931, which asserts that two bodies in equilibrium with a third are in equilibrium with each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ralph H Fowler.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics states that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.

 

• The term “zeroth law” was coined by British physicist Ralph H. Fowler in 1931, after the first, second and third laws had already been established — hence the need for a law numbered “zero” to precede them logically. (शून्यवाँ नियम — राल्फ फाउलर)

 

• This law provides the basis for the concept of temperature and for the use of thermometers as a means of comparing the thermal states of different systems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Law of Thermodynamics deals with conservation of energy; the Second Law introduces entropy; the Third Law concerns absolute zero.

 

NOTE

 

• James Clerk Maxwell (Option 1): Known for Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism and the kinetic theory of gases, not for naming the zeroth law.

 

• Max Planck (Option 2): Known as the founder of quantum theory (Planck's constant), not for naming the zeroth law.

 

• Josiah Willard Gibbs (Option 3): Known for contributions to chemical thermodynamics and statistical mechanics (Gibbs free energy), not for naming the zeroth law.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in capital receipts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taxes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Capital receipts are government receipts that either create a liability or reduce assets, and include items such as borrowings, recovery of loans, disinvestment proceeds, and foreign aid/loans. (कर — राजस्व प्राप्ति, पूंजीगत प्राप्ति नहीं)

 

• Taxes (direct taxes like income tax, and indirect taxes like GST) are classified as revenue receipts, since they neither create a liability nor lead to a reduction in government assets — they are recurring receipts used to meet normal government expenditure.

 

• Since taxes do not fit the definition of capital receipts, they are the correct “NOT included” answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Revenue receipts include tax revenue and non-tax revenue (interest receipts, dividends, fees, fines).

 

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 aims to ensure fiscal discipline by regulating the government's reliance on capital receipts like borrowings.

 

NOTE

 

• Foreign aid (Option 1): Loans/grants from foreign governments/institutions are treated as capital receipts (they create a liability or are non-recurring).

 

• Recovery of loans (Option 3): A capital receipt because it reduces government assets (outstanding loans given by the government).

 

• Borrowings (Option 4): A capital receipt because it creates a liability (debt) for the government.

question: What is the name of the portal launched by the Government in 2022 that aims to ease the loan application and disbursement process by the applicant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jan Samarth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jan Samarth Portal was launched by the Government of India in 2022 as a National Portal for Credit-Linked Government Schemes. (जन समर्थ पोर्टल — ऋण आवेदन)

 

• It is a digital, paperless platform that connects lenders (banks) with government scheme databases, aiming to simplify and speed up the loan application, approval and disbursement process for beneficiaries of various government credit-linked schemes.

 

• It covers loan schemes across categories such as education loans, agriculture infrastructure loans, business/livelihood loans, and self-employment loans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The portal was formally launched around 6 June 2022, integrating multiple credit-linked schemes onto a single digital platform.

 

NOTE

 

• Swayatta (Option 1): Not a real government loan portal name; a distractor option.

 

• E-Shram (Option 3): A portal launched in 2021 to create a national database of unorganised sector workers, not specifically a loan-disbursement portal.

 

• Yukti (Option 4): A UGC/AICTE innovation and start-up platform for higher education institutions, unrelated to loan disbursement.

question: In which year did Narendra Modi propose to celebrate a day for yoga as ‘International Day of Yoga’ while speaking at the United Nations General Assembly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed the idea of an ‘International Day of Yoga’ in his address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on 27 September 2014. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय योग दिवस — प्रस्ताव 2014)

 

• Following this, the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution on 11 December 2014, declaring 21 June as the International Day of Yoga, with support from a record 177 co-sponsoring countries.

 

• The first International Day of Yoga was celebrated on 21 June 2015.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• 21 June was chosen as it is the Summer Solstice, the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, considered significant in the yogic tradition.

 

• The theme and mass yoga demonstrations, including at Kartavya Path/Rajpath, New Delhi, mark the day's celebration every year.

 

NOTE

 

• 2013 (Option 1): Too early; Modi's UNGA proposal came in 2014.

 

• 2015 (Option 2): This is the year the first International Day of Yoga was celebrated, not the year it was proposed.

 

• 2016 (Option 3): Not connected to either the proposal or the first celebration of the day.

question: What would happen if the difference in pressure in Tahiti was negative?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Below average and late monsoon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Southern Oscillation (SO) refers to the periodic reversal of pressure conditions between the eastern Pacific (Tahiti) and the western Pacific/Indian Ocean side (Darwin, Australia), and is closely linked to the Indian monsoon. (दक्षिणी दोलन — ताहिती-डार्विन दाब अंतर)

 

• Meteorologists monitor the pressure difference between Tahiti and Darwin to compute the Southern Oscillation Index (SOI), used to predict monsoon behaviour in India.

 

• When this pressure difference is negative (i.e., pressure is relatively lower over Tahiti, associated with El Niño conditions), the monsoon rainfall over India tends to be below average and delayed (late) in onset.

 

• Conversely, when the SO is positive (higher pressure over Tahiti than Darwin, associated with La Niña-like conditions), India tends to receive good/above-average rainfall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• El Niño events (warming of the central/eastern Pacific) are generally correlated with weak monsoons in India, while La Niña events are associated with strong monsoons.

 

NOTE

 

• Above average late monsoon (Option 1): Incorrect combination — a negative pressure difference is linked with below-average, not above-average, rainfall.

 

• Drought (Option 2): Too extreme/imprecise a description compared to the textbook relationship of “below average and late” monsoon.

 

• Above average and early monsoon (Option 4): Incorrect — this describes the effect of a positive (not negative) pressure difference.

question: In which year was an approach and program named Joint Forest Management (JFM) launched in the context of National Forest Policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1988.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Forest Policy, 1988 marked a major shift in India's forestry approach, emphasising conservation, environmental stability, and involvement of local communities in forest management. (संयुक्त वन प्रबंधन — 1988)

 

• In this context, the approach/programme of Joint Forest Management (JFM) was launched in 1988, aiming to involve local communities and forest departments as partners in protecting, regenerating and managing forest resources, in exchange for a share of forest produce/benefits.

 

• JFM was later formalised nationally through a Government of India circular in June 1990, encouraging states to adopt JFM resolutions and set up Forest Protection Committees / JFM Committees.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The pioneering example of community-forest department cooperation, the Arabari experiment in West Bengal (early 1970s–80s), is often cited as a precursor to formal JFM.

 

• JFM represented a shift from a purely regulatory, revenue-oriented forest policy to a participatory, welfare-oriented approach.

 

NOTE

 

• 1965 (Option 1): Not associated with the launch of JFM or the National Forest Policy.

 

• 1996 (Option 3): Not the year of JFM's launch; by 1996 JFM programmes were already being implemented in several states.

 

• 1947 (Option 4): The year of India's independence, unrelated to the launch of JFM.

question: Which Session of Congress and Muslim League reached an understanding of creating a joint front against the British regime?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lucknow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Lucknow Session of December 1916, the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League held a joint session and reached the historic “Lucknow Pact”. (लखनऊ अधिवेशन 1916 — लखनऊ पैक्ट)

 

• Under the pact, both organisations agreed on a scheme of constitutional reforms to present to the British government and, notably, agreed on separate electorates for Muslims along with a formula for representation.

 

• The pact marked a rare period of Hindu-Muslim unity and a joint front against British rule, and was also the session at which the Congress split of 1907 (Moderates-Extremists) was healed, with Bal Gangadhar Tilak rejoining the Congress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lucknow Session of Congress in 1916 was presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar; the Muslim League session was led by figures including Muhammad Ali Jinnah, who played a key role in brokering the pact.

 

• The Lucknow Pact influenced the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act, 1919).

 

NOTE

 

• Bombay (Option 1): Site of the Congress session of 1885 (first session) and later the Quit India Resolution (1942), not the Congress-League joint front understanding.

 

• Allahabad (Option 2): Site of the Muslim League session (1930) where Muhammad Iqbal proposed a separate Muslim state, not the joint Congress-League pact.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): Site of various Congress sessions, but not the one where the Congress-League joint understanding (Lucknow Pact) was reached.
